html:
The Charter of Ban Kulin is a trade agreement of 29 August 1189 in which Kulin, the ban or ruler of Bosnia, granted the merchants of Dubrovnik the right to trade freely in his lands without paying duties.

Written in the Bosnian form of Cyrillic in the local Slavic speech, it is one of the oldest state documents of the South Slavs and the oldest from Bosnia. Kulin's long rule was later remembered as a golden age of peace and plenty. The charter tied Bosnia's silver and lead mines and its trade routes to the merchants of the Republic of Ragusa, a link that lasted for centuries. In Kulin's time the pope accused Bosnia of heresy, the first sign of the Bosnian Church.
